scope: bounded operator-valued Schur-Herglotz responses on separable Hilbert space, real-axis nontangential boundary values, scalarization and topology-labelled operator upgrades

strongestTheorem.measureLevel: The positive operator-valued representing measure is canonical and retains absolutely continuous, atomic and singular-continuous parts.
strongestTheorem.almostEverywhere: On a common full-measure set obtained from a countable dense family and polarization, scalar matrix elements have nontangential boundary values; Im M/pi is the Radon-Nikodym density as a scalar form wherever finite.
strongestTheorem.operatorLevel: A WOT/SOT/norm boundary operator exists only when uniform boundedness and convergence are proved in that topology.
strongestTheorem.schurLevel: Boundary and Schur elimination commute in norm under an invertible limiting denominator, or strongly under strong-* factor convergence plus a uniform inverse bound.

dispatcher.refusal: never replace Sigma by only its a.e. density

dispatcher.output: apply the a.e. boundary theorem on vertical or nontangential paths; preserve arbitrary tangential paths as arc data
dispatcher.refusal: do not promote a nontangential limit to every path

dispatcher.output: commute boundary limit with Schur in norm, or in strong-* with a uniform inverse bound

frontiers.reentryCondition: Declare closed operators, common form domains, graph topology and domain transport under adjoints and Schur elimination.
Choose a Hamiltonian/PDE, threshold set and weighted or Besov operator scale, then prove a uniform resolvent estimate.
Include boundary values of off-diagonal blocks and a replacement passivity identity.

boundedBoundaryExhaustion.reason: Measure type, approach geometry, operator topology, inverse control, Schur multiplicativity, principal value, spectral scaling and nonuniform tails are independently routed; remaining questions require new domain, model, coupling or nonlinear structure.
